pages.text:
Devanshi Shah
CE BTech 2022 VJTI
MSCI | FTE Interview | On-Campus
MSCI had come at the start of the 2021 placement drive. There were 3 rounds scheduled
beforehand: online test, technical interview and managerial interview. All three of them were on
different days. CE, IT and circuit branch students pursuing their bachelors, CE Masters and MCA
students having CGPA greater than 6 were allowed to apply.
ROUND 1: ONLINE TEST (70 mins)
Date: 5th August, 2021
It was at 6.00 pm on HackerRank. There was a 90 min window to start the test.
There were 16 MCQs and 1 coding question. The MCQs were related to CS fundamentals, output
prediction and logic. There was no negative marking.
Coding question: Caesar Edit Distance
You’re given two strings. You’ve to return the minimum cost of converting one string to another.
To change a string, you can insert, replace or delete any character. Each of these operations has
cost 1. This is regular Edit Distance problem. However, the twist was that you can shift all
characters of a string by any constant amount without any cost. For example “abcd” can be
converted to “bcde” or “lmno” or “pqrs” without any cost.
Sample input: “aeiou”, “bfjqx”
Sample output: 2
Explanation: aeiou -> bfjpv: cost=0; bfjpv -> bfjqx: cost=2 (2 replacements)
It was not necessary to solve the coding question to get shortlisted because the MCQs had good
weightage as well. But then you have to be sure about your MCQs.
The interviews were scheduled the next day 4 pm onwards. 39 students were shortlisted. Further
rounds were held on Microsoft teams. (It’s recommended that you keep the desktop app installed
and download the app on your phone as well, just in case)
ROUND 2: TECHNICAL INTERVIEW (45 mins)
Date: 6th August, 2021

The interviewer was extremely polite, unlike many.
He initiated the meeting by introducing himself followed by my introduction and a brief idea
about my projects. I explained my internship project, my role in it and a hint of difficulties that I
had faced.
Note: Be prepared with your introduction beforehand. You can drive the conversation in the
direction you want by highlighting certain things in your introduction. Also, be thoroughly
prepared with your resume.
In my internship, I had worked on the frontend where we had used Angular and the interviewer
had 6 years of experience in frontend development. So I was cross-questioned on that.
Questions like
1.
How does Angular improve performance?
2.
What is a Virtual DOM?
3.
How differently does Virtual DOM work as compared to Real DOM?
DSA:
https://www.interviewbit.com/problems/simplify-directory-path/
He asked me to share my screen and open notepad. After explaining the approach, he asked me
to code the solution (Not pseudo code). I was coding in C++ and had used stack and string from
STL. Once I was done, I was asked to walk him through the solution. He asked me about handling
different corner cases and wanted to test it for a sample test case. I had missed out one or two
things which I added afterwards. He asked about the time and space complexity.
Note: Be aware of internal working, time and space complexity of any inbuilt methods or data
structures that you use.
OS:
He asked me about paging. I explained to him about virtual memory and situations in which
pagination occurs. He gave me a scenario.
Q. There are two devices with 2GB RAM and 16GB RAM. 3GB memory is needed by a process to
be executed. There are no other processes. Will paging be used? When?
I said that it will be used in case of the device with 2GB RAM and explained further. Then he
asked if there will be any scenario where there'll be pagination despite the 16GB RAM? I thought
for a moment and said that I can’t think of any such scenario. He said okay and moved on.
Note: I searched hard afterwards and this might be the answer to the 16GB RAM question.
DBMS:

Started with standard questions like
1.
Types of databases (The answer is not SQL and NoSQL:))
2.
Examples of non-relational databases
3.
Explain atomicity (try to explain concepts with example)
4.
Choice of database in some application where atomicity is not important
5.
CRUD principle
He asked me if I had any questions for him in response to which I questioned him from his
introduction earlier. (Why should interviewers have all the fun :P)
We got the mail about the next round the same night with 23 students shortlisted.
ROUND 3: MANAGERIAL INTERVIEW (45 mins)
Date: 9th August, 2021
This round was scheduled two days after the first interview. One of the things that I liked about
MSCI was how well-organised their recruitment process was. There were no precipitous
decisions or last moment interviews. It saved us a lot of anxiety. The interviews started at 4 pm.
I had a female interviewer this time who also was very sweet and polite and started by
introducing herself. Then she moved towards my introduction and recent projects. I had a
freelance project, an internship project and a few others. So discussion of these took a major
chunk of the time.
1.
Explain the projects and mainly my role in them
2.
How was my freelance project experience different from the one at a corporate
organisation
3.
Something new apart from technical stuff that I learnt in each of them
4.
Was deployment part of any project?
5.
How do you improve a website’s performance? And some technical questions around that
6.
What do you think of Agile Methodology?
7.
Anything you want to say apart from what you’ve mentioned till now? (I mentioned that I’m
interning at a startup. I got a few follow up questions on this.)
It felt more like a conversation than an interview. Being confident and pitching yourself in the
right way is important. I didn’t realise when an hour had passed. She had asked many more
questions so be prepared with your stories.
She concluded by asking if I had any questions for her.

This round was great and I was done by 5 pm. I knew that there were no further rounds but I was
prepared and waiting for any update that might follow. I had interviews for one more company
that day as well so everything added up to a lot of perturbation.
At 7.45 pm (when I had almost lost all hope) I received an email about an HR discussion at 8 pm. I
sprang from my seat. Then I got to know that 6 of us were their final selects and we had an HR
discussion (where nothing could go wrong :P)
LAST MINUTE ADVICE (kyuki prepare to kar hi liya hoga :))
1.
Go through company archives to understand the pattern.
2.
Research about the company (for managerial or HR rounds and to understand if you
would actually like to work for them, benefits aside).
3.
Ask GOOD questions at the end. Show your interest.
4.
You will never be prepared enough and you can’t possibly know all the answers. It’s okay
to goof up, let it go. Do what’s in your hand and leave the rest to destiny.
5.
It’s good to be nervous, but don’t show it. Be confident and don’t forget to smile :)
RESOURCES WHICH HELPED ME
1.
Yash Jain ka Repo (This is GOLD)
2.
Must Do Questions on GFG
3.
450 DSA by Love Babbar
4.
Make a list of topics in each subject that you want to cover and watch videos or read
about those topics. Don’t forget to cover examples and problems on those topics as well.
Resources for this are vague (mostly YT and GFG)
All the best!
